messages:
maria nguyen: heads up — SLO alert just fired for ingress: 5xx ratio + p95 latency. multiple customer tickets referencing timeouts and 502s. raising an incident thread to collect repros and narrow root cause. :rotating_light:

sre-bot: Alert: ingress.slo.5xx_ratio > 0.02 for 5m, p95 latency 1200ms (>900ms SLO) — viz: https://grafana/redwood/d/ingress

olivia patel: seeing chatter in support too. customers A and B reported timeouts between 08:01–08:12 UTC with request-ids. forwarding sample request IDs to thread: req=abc123, req=def456

ashok rao: grabbing traces now. quick check — authz-token-service is returning 502s to the edge at the same time window. running query: 
```
# ClickHouse: count of 5xx by upstream
SELECT upstream_service, count() AS errors
FROM http_logs
WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 15 minute
  AND status >= 500
GROUP BY upstream_service
ORDER BY errors DESC
LIMIT 10
```

ashok rao: results: authz-token-service 48, billing-service 12, model-proxy 3. authz seems dominant.

lee chen: can we confirm trace span gaps? I'm seeing a cluster of edges with no downstream spans (trace incomplete) — possible sampling or dropped spans from the authz side. Querying traces for req=abc123...

lee chen: trace shows edge->authz call lasts ~700ms then a 502 at authz. interestingly authz logs show timeouts trying to reach a downstream payment-vendor during that window.

frank gilmore: payment-vendor had transient 5xx earlier — ops on payments ops reported brief degradation at 08:05 UTC. looks correlated. are we shadowing external vendor outage into authz?

maria nguyen: good catch. support thread mentions billing metadata fetch failing which authz relies on. that could cascade to timeout while token validation waits for billing lookup.

olivia patel: customers seeing 502 from our API — they'd attribute to our service. we need clear repro steps and a short mitigation (fallback) path to reduce SLO burn. Suggestions?

ashok rao: short term: add an automatic fallback in authz to bypass billing check for critical paths (return cached billing status or default) and set a circuit-breaker to fail fast instead of waiting for external vendor. can we deploy a 10% canary?

maria nguyen: agree. Lee, can you test a local patch that adds a 200ms timeout to billing calls and returns cached value on timeout? If logs look good, we can push a canary.

lee chen: on it. repro steps I'm running locally: 
```
# reproduce the slow path with curl to edge with a simulated slow billing backend
curl -H "x-test-billing-delay: 600" -H "x-request-id: abc123" https://edge.redwood/api/v1/generate -v
```

lee chen: local run shows edge receives 502 after authz waits 600ms then errors. after applying local timeout patch (200ms) edge returns 200 with cached-billing header. sending logs in thread.

support-bot: Ticket 4321 linked: customer B reported 502s at 08:06 UTC, req=def456. Status: escalated -> engineering.

ashok rao: prepping deploy. plan: authz patch -> 10% canary -> monitor 5xx and p95 for 10m -> increase rollout if stable. rolling back path ready.

maria nguyen: create grafana panel updates and a temporary dashboard monitoring: ingress 5xx, authz 502s, billing latency, external vendor 5xx, traces missing spans. include alert to mute noisy src if we deploy fallback.

lee chen: here are the log snippets from authz around req=abc123 (sanitized):
```
[08:05:12] authz INFO req=abc123 billing.lookup start
[08:05:12] authz WARN req=abc123 billing.lookup timeout after 600ms
[08:05:12] authz ERROR req=abc123 upstream=payment-vendor status=502 body="Bad Gateway"
[08:05:12] authz INFO req=abc123 returning 502 to edge
```

frank gilmore: ops on payments confirmed spike at 08:05–08:07 due to vendor's rolling deploy. they've opened vendor ticket and reverted. vendor claims deploy caused transient DB connection saturation.

olivia patel: we should update support messages: explain transient downstream vendor outage causing authz errors and that we're rolling a fallback to reduce impact while vendor reverts. also send ETA for canary.

maria nguyen: can someone prepare a short customer notification draft? I'll sign off.

ashok rao: canary is up (10%) — monitor link: https://grafana/redwood/d/ingress?var-canary=10

sre-bot: Canary deployment started: authz-fallback v1.2 -> 10% of edge traffic.

lee chen: initial canary metrics: authz 502s down 80% for canary buckets, ingress p95 dropping from 1200ms -> 650ms for canary. overall infra 5xx still high because canary fraction small.

maria nguyen: if metrics keep improving, increase to 50% in 5m. frank coordinating with payments ops to confirm vendor rollback complete.

support-bot: customer-notice draft: "We observed increased 502 errors between 08:01–08:12 UTC caused by a downstream payments vendor issue that impacted our authz path. We’ve deployed a temporary fallback to reduce impact while vendor reverts. We will follow up after full postmortem."

olivia patel: looks good, send after 50% canary check.

ashok rao: increasing canary to 50% now.

sre-bot: Canary scaled to 50%. Monitoring for 15m.

lee chen: after scale, overall ingress 5xx ratio dropped from 2.4% -> 0.3% and p95 down to 320ms. SLO burn trending back under threshold.

maria nguyen: excellent. closing immediate escalation. please file a postmortem with timeline, root cause (vendor deploy), why authz didn't fail fast, and actions (circuit-breaker, cached-billing, improved observability on trace gaps). assign to ashok + lee + frank.

frank gilmore: filing a vendor incident link and attaching vendor ticket ID. I'll include vendor communication and rollback timeline.

olivia patel: I'll follow up with support communication and customer list.

maria nguyen: thanks team. leave this thread open for postmortem drafts and small follow-ups. :thumbsup:
